1/6 A callee can regain control before a contract's first function call finishes, allowing repeated use of stale state.

2/6 This occurs when state updates happen after an external call rather than before it.

3/6 The standard remedy is to perform internal state changes prior to any external interaction.

4/6 Alternatively, developers may implement a reentrancy lock to block unwanted callbacks into the protected path.

5/6 A lock prevents control from returning to the caller while the callee is executing.

6/6 However, a lock does not stop the external callee from passing control back to the original contract.
